item.title: ANURUP: privacy-first photo and PDF tools
item.description:
Open the app · Wiki · GitHub Repo

Overview

Government exam, job, visa and KYC portals each want something slightly different: a 35×45 mm photo under 50 KB, a signature at 140×60 px, one merged PDF under 500 KB. ANURUP is a free set of photo and PDF tools for exactly these uploads.

It runs in the browser, so your files never leave your device, and there is no account to create. It works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on a computer or a phone, and you can install it as an app that keeps working offline.

All tools

Each tool has its own address, so you can bookmark the ones you use most.

Photo and signature PDF
Passport Size Photo Maker PDF Viewer
Resize Image to KB & Pixels JPG to PDF Converter
Compress Image to KB Merge PDF
Crop, Rotate & Flip Image Split PDF
Remove Image Background Organize PDF Pages
Signature Cleaner Compress PDF to KB
JPG, PNG & WebP Converter PDF to JPG / PNG
Add Page Numbers & Watermark
Sign & Fill PDF
Remove PDF Password

How it works

  1. Pick a tool on the home page, or search for the task, for example 50 KB, signature, merge or password.
  2. Drop a file on the upload box, click to browse, or paste an image with Ctrl/⌘+V.
  3. Change the settings and click the main button. The result shows up below with a preview.
  4. Download it, or send it straight to another tool.

Chaining tools

A form upload usually takes more than one step. Every result has a Continue with this file row that opens the file in the next tool, so you don’t have to download it and upload it again. Some common chains:

  • Crop → Remove background → Passport photo → Resize to KB
  • Signature Cleaner → Resize to KB → Sign & Fill PDF
  • JPG to PDF → Compress PDF
  • Remove PDF Password → Merge PDF → Compress PDF

Files you pass along, or save with Save to workspace, land in the Workspace. It’s a shared tray that survives a page refresh and holds up to 60 files. Any upload box can pick from it, and you can select several files and send them to Merge PDF or JPG to PDF in one go.

Privacy

ANURUP is a static website on GitHub Pages. Every tool runs inside your browser tab with Canvas, pdf-lib, PDF.js and QPDF compiled to WebAssembly, so no server ever receives your photos, PDFs or passwords.

The page downloads three things: the app itself, web fonts from Google Fonts and, the first time you use Remove Image Background, its AI model from IMG.LY’s CDN. Your photo is still processed on your device.

The browser keeps your workspace files (in IndexedDB), your light or dark choice (in localStorage) and a copy of the app for offline use. A PDF password is used once to decrypt the file and isn’t stored anywhere. Remove PDF Password also needs the real password. It doesn’t guess or crack anything.

Install and use offline

ANURUP is a Progressive Web App. Once installed, it opens in its own window from the dock, Start menu or home screen.

Where How
Chrome or Edge on a computer Click Install app in the sidebar, or the install icon in the address bar
Android (Chrome) Tap the download icon in the top bar, or Install app in the menu
iPhone and iPad (Safari) Share → Add to Home Screen
Safari on a Mac File → Add to Dock

After your first visit the app keeps a copy of itself (about 6 MB), and every tool works without internet, installed or not. Remove Image Background is the one exception: it downloads its AI model the first time and works offline after that. When a new version is out, ANURUP shows a Reload prompt. Nothing changes until you click it, so a tool won’t reset in the middle of a job.

Under the hood

Part What it uses
Interface React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI
PDF pdf-lib, PDF.js, and QPDF compiled to WebAssembly for removing passwords
Images Canvas, and IMG.LY’s background-removal model running on the device
Build Vite, plus a prerender step that writes a static page for every tool, a sitemap and a 404 page
Offline vite-plugin-pwa and a Workbox service worker
Tests Vitest
Hosting GitHub Pages, deployed by GitHub Actions on every push to main

Guides

The ANURUP wiki has step-by-step guides:

  • Getting started: how the app is laid out and how to move a file from one tool to the next
  • Install as an app: add it to your dock or home screen, update it, uninstall it
  • Photo and signature guides: resize a photo to 20-50 KB, make a passport size photo, prepare a signature for an exam form, change a background to white
  • PDF guides: JPG to PDF, compress a PDF to 100 KB, merge certificates, remove the password from a bank statement or e-Aadhaar, sign a form
  • Workspace and chaining: keep files between tools without downloading them
  • Privacy and security: what stays on your device and what the app downloads
  • FAQ and Troubleshooting
  • Development: run it locally, add a tool, deploy

Found a bug? Open an issue with the tool name, your browser and what you expected to happen. Please don’t attach private documents.

item.title: Diff Checker: In-Browser Text and Jupyter Notebook Comparisons
item.description:
Open Diff Checker

Overview

Comparing files often means pasting proprietary code or data into online tools that upload your text to external servers. Standard diff viewers also struggle with structured formats like Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb), where minor metadata or execution counts obscure the actual code changes.

Diff Checker is a fast, web-based comparison tool designed to solve both problems. It handles plain text, source code, and Jupyter notebooks entirely inside your browser tab. Your files never leave your computer, no account is required, and the application works offline as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA).

Text and Code Comparison

The text comparison engine handles raw text, scripts, configuration files, and documentation with multiple viewing modes and customization options:

  • Split and Unified Views: Toggle between a two-column side-by-side view and a single-column unified diff view with a single keypress (u).
  • Granular Highlighting: Choose between character-level, word-level, and line-level difference highlighting to spot single-character edits or large structural shifts.
  • Diff Normalization: Toggle options to ignore whitespace discrepancies, ignore case variations, skip blank lines, or ignore carriage return line endings (\r\n vs \n).
  • Swap Panes: Switch the original and modified inputs with one click to reverse the comparison direction.
  • Patch Export: Generate and copy standard unified diff patches ready to apply with git apply or patch.

Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) Diffing

Jupyter notebooks store code, rendered outputs, and execution metadata together in a JSON structure. A standard diff tool often shows dozens of meaningless changes when all you did was run a cell.

Diff Checker parses the notebook structure to deliver cell-level diffs:

Feature How Diff Checker handles it
Cell Separation Groups changes by Markdown cells and Code cells instead of raw JSON lines.
Cell Movement Detects when a cell has been moved up or down within the notebook.
Noisy Metadata Filtering Ignores execution counts, cell collapse states, and execution timestamps that create false diffs.
Rich Output Comparison Compares cell outputs including plain text, stdout, stderr, HTML tables, and embedded images (PNG, JPEG, SVG).
Fallback Plaintext Mode Allows switching back to raw text comparison if a notebook contains malformed JSON.

Privacy and Local Execution

Diff Checker is hosted as a static site on GitHub Pages:

  • Zero Server Uploads: All diff parsing and Myers difference algorithms run locally in client-side JavaScript.
  • Background Processing: Large files and notebooks are processed inside dedicated Web Workers so the browser UI remains responsive.
  • No Tracking: No analytics cookies, trackers, or third-party tracking scripts are loaded.
  • Strict Content Security Policy: The site enforces strict HTTP headers restricting scripts and network requests to local origins.

Keyboard Shortcuts

The interface is built for keyboard-first navigation:

Key Action
n / p Jump to next or previous difference chunk
j / k Jump to next or previous notebook cell
u Toggle between unified and split views
Ctrl + Enter / Cmd + Enter Run the diff comparison
? Display keyboard shortcuts guide
Esc Close dialogs, drawers, and modal overlays

Shortcuts pause automatically while your cursor is inside an active text input area.

Install and Offline Support

Diff Checker is configured as a Progressive Web App (PWA). Once you load the page in Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox, the application assets cache in the browser. You can install it directly to your dock or home screen, and it will continue functioning without an active internet connection.

Under the Hood

Layer Technologies
Framework & UI Svelte 5, TypeScript, Modern CSS
Build Tool Vite, with vite-plugin-pwa and Workbox service workers
Diff Engine Myers diff algorithm implementation with Web Worker offloading
Notebook Parsing In-browser nbformat 4 JSON parser with rich output decoding
Hosting GitHub Pages via automated GitHub Actions deployment

item.title: NSEScraper: An Open-Source Scraper for nseindia.com
item.description:
PyPI Package · GitHub Repository

Overview

The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) website provides live market feeds, but extracting clean intraday price histories for quantitative analysis or algorithmic backtesting often requires navigating session headers, cookie rotation, and nested JSON endpoints.

nsescraper is a lightweight, open-source Python library that queries NSE endpoints directly and returns cleaned, timestamped pandas DataFrames for any listed index or equity. It supports standard 1-minute OHLC bars, custom multi-minute intervals, and second-by-second tick data.

Installation

Install the package directly from PyPI using pip:

1

pip install nsescraper

Dependencies: Python 3.8+ and pandas.

Features

  • Real-time Intraday Feeds: Extract the current trading day’s prices for indices (Nifty 50, Bank Nifty, Midcap, Sectoral indices) and all NSE-listed stocks.
  • 1-Minute OHLC Candles: Formats timestamped Open, High, Low, and Close bars across the full market session.
  • 1-Second Tick Data: Capture granular tick-level price changes throughout active market hours.
  • Custom Candlestick Resampling: Parameterize candle intervals to custom durations (e.g., 5-minute, 15-minute, or 60-minute bars).
  • Direct pandas Integration: Every function returns a standard pandas DataFrame ready for technical analysis, plotting, or CSV export.

item.title: Brain Tumour Classification
item.description:
GitHub Repository · Jupyter Notebook

Overview

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the primary non-invasive modality for diagnosing intracranial tumors. However, differentiating between tumor subtypes on axial MRI slices is challenging due to variable lesion margins, necrotic tissue regions, and subtle intensity differences between abnormal and healthy neural tissue.

This project implements a transfer learning pipeline in PyTorch, fine-tuning a VGG16 convolutional neural network to categorize brain MRI scans into four distinct diagnostic categories.

The Diagnostic Classes

The classification model evaluates MRI slices across three major intracranial tumor categories alongside healthy control scans:

Class Pathological Profile
Glioma Primary brain tumors arising from glial cells, typically presenting irregular, infiltrative boundaries.
Meningioma Usually slow-growing tumors arising from the meningeal membranes enveloping the brain and spinal cord.
Pituitary Tumors originating in the pituitary gland at the base of the skull, frequently affecting hormonal pathways.
No Tumor Control scans exhibiting normal cerebral anatomy without focal space-occupying lesions.

Preprocessing & Image Augmentation

MRI scans vary significantly in intensity, resolution, and skull orientation across clinical imaging centers. Using OpenCV and PyTorch torchvision transforms, each image undergoes standardized preprocessing:

  • Contour-Based Brain Cropping: Detects the largest contour in the grayscale image to isolate the cranial region, removing black border margins and non-informative background pixels.
  • Standardization: Resizes images to $224 \times 224$ pixels and normalizes pixel values against standard ImageNet channel means and standard deviations.
  • Data Augmentation: To prevent overfitting on small clinical sample cohorts, the training pipeline applies:
    • Random horizontal and vertical flips
    • Random affine rotations ($\pm 15^\circ$)
    • Random scaling and perspective shifts
    • Brightness and contrast adjustments

Model Architecture & Transfer Learning

Instead of training a deep convolutional network from scratch on a limited medical dataset, the pipeline adapts VGG16 pre-trained on ImageNet:

  1. Feature Extractor: Frozen early convolutional blocks retain low-level visual primitives (edges, gradients, textures).
  2. Fine-Tuning: The deeper convolutional layers are unfrozen with a reduced learning rate to learn domain-specific neuroimaging patterns.
  3. Custom Classification Head: Replaces VGG16’s original 1000-class classifier with:
    • Adaptive Average Pooling
    • Dense Layer (512 units) with ReLU activation
    • Dropout ($p = 0.5$) for regularization
    • Final Linear Layer (4 output units) mapped through Softmax

Optimization & Experimentation

We benchmarked four optimization algorithms to assess convergence stability and loss reduction:

  • Adam: Provided the fastest initial convergence and stable training progression using adaptive moment estimation.
  • SGD with Momentum ($0.9$): Exhibited smoother gradient trajectories and achieved competitive final test accuracy when paired with a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler.
  • RMSprop & AdaGrad: Evaluated as adaptive baselines, though RMSprop showed occasional loss oscillations on smaller batch sizes.

Results & Diagnostic Evaluation

Model performance was evaluated on a held-out test split using multi-class metrics:

  • Confusion Matrix Analysis: Evaluates class-specific misclassifications, prioritizing high sensitivity on glioma scans to avoid missed high-grade lesions.
  • Per-Class Precision, Recall, and F1-Score: Ensures consistent diagnostic performance across both common and rarer tumor presentations without class bias.

The complete training scripts, hyperparameter configurations, and evaluation graphs are documented in the project notebook.

item.title: Forecasting and Anomaly Detection
item.description:
GitHub Repository

Overview

Retail demand forecasting requires balancing macroeconomic indicators, regional promotional events, and seasonal holidays. At the same time, unexpected sales spikes or drops need to be isolated to separate genuine demand shifts from supply chain bottlenecks or data collection errors.

This project uses the historical Walmart sales dataset (covering 45 stores across diverse regions) to benchmark multiple forecasting approaches and evaluate unsupervised anomaly detection techniques on retail time series.

Dataset & Feature Engineering

The dataset tracks weekly department-level sales alongside store attributes and regional economic indicators:

  • Temporal Signals: Week of year, month, and major holiday indicators (Super Bowl, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas).
  • Store Characteristics: Store type (A, B, C) and store size.
  • Macroeconomic Factors: Regional Consumer Price Index (CPI), unemployment rates, and local fuel prices.
  • Promotions: Anonymized markdown discounts (MarkDown1 through MarkDown5).

Preprocessing included forward-filling missing markdown values, cyclical encoding of week numbers, and scaling continuous economic variables.

Forecasting Models

We evaluated several regression and time series models on held-out test periods:

Linear & Regularized Regression

  • Multiple Linear Regression: Established a baseline mapping features directly to weekly revenue.
  • Polynomial Feature Expansion: Captured non-linear interactions between weather (temperature), holiday proximity, and markdown events.
  • L1 & L2 Regularization (Lasso, Ridge, Elastic Net): Penalized collinear features—particularly among markdowns and store size tiers—to control overfitting and improve test set generalization.

Time Series Forecasting

  • ARMA / ARIMA: Modeled the sequential auto-regressive structure and moving averages on stationary, differenced weekly sales series to capture recurring annual seasonality.

Anomaly Detection Approaches

To identify unusual sales swings without labeled incident logs, we applied three unsupervised techniques:

  • k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) Distance: Evaluates each data point’s Euclidean distance to its $k$-th nearest neighbor in feature space. Samples with large neighborhood distances represent rare sales conditions.
  • DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering): Groups dense clusters of regular sales activity while isolating points in low-density regions as noise/anomalies.
  • LSTM Autoencoders: Sequences of weekly sales were passed through an LSTM encoder-decoder architecture trained exclusively on typical demand patterns. High reconstruction errors flag non-standard anomalies where sales deviate sharply from temporal expectations.

Data Version Control (DVC)

To keep model weights, intermediate data splits, and feature matrices reproducible across runs without committing multi-megabyte CSVs into Git, the project uses Data Version Control (DVC). DVC tracks pointer files in Git while storing large artifacts in remote storage, making every experiment pipeline reproducible from raw data to evaluation metrics.

item.title: Paris Summer Olympic Games 2024 Dashboard
item.description:
GitHub Repository · Kaggle Dataset

Overview

The Paris 2024 Summer Olympic Games featured over 10,500 athletes competing across 32 sports and 329 medal events. This Power BI dashboard aggregates competition records into interactive views exploring country medal tallies, gender parity in podium finishes, individual athlete records, and multi-year historical trends.

The report contains five interconnected pages with dynamic cross-filtering by sport, country, and event.

Dashboard Pages

1. Home & Navigation

The landing screen provides a high-level visual intro and direct navigation links across the four core analytical modules.

2. Medal Overview & Geographic Distribution

This page summarizes total medal counts, gold-to-bronze distributions, and global medal density.

  • Medals by Country & Gender: Stacked bar charts showing the balance of medals won by male and female athletes across participating nations.
  • Choropleth Map: Visualizes medal density worldwide, highlighting regional strongholds in specific athletic disciplines.
  • Game-Wise Slicers: Allows filtering all charts simultaneously by selecting individual sports (e.g., Athletics, Swimming, Gymnastics).

3. Athlete Performance & Disciplines

A dedicated athlete directory exploring individual performances, multiple medalists, and sport-specific achievements.

  • Athlete Roster: Searchable table listing athletes with their nationality, events entered, and medal outcomes.
  • Multi-Medal Winners: Highlights top competitors who secured podium placements across multiple individual or team events.
  • Filters: Drill down by country, sporting discipline, gender, or medal type.

4. Country Profiles

An in-depth breakdown of individual National Olympic Committees (NOCs) and their medal composition.

  • National Leaderboard: Compares official IOC ranking (sorted by gold medal priority) with total medal count.
  • Discipline Strengths: Identifies which sports contributed the largest share of a country’s total medal haul.
  • Podium Conversion: Visualizes the ratio of finals reached to medals won.

5. Historical Context & Multi-Games Trends

Places Paris 2024 in context by comparing national performance against historical Olympic Games.

  • Historical Medal Trajectories: Line charts tracking how nations have trended over multiple modern Olympic editions.
  • Emerging Contenders: Flags countries achieving their first-ever Olympic medals or record-high medal totals in 2024.

Key DAX Measures

  • Total Medals: COUNTROWS(Medals)
  • Gold Medal Ratio: DIVIDE(CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Medals), Medals[Medal] = "Gold"), [Total Medals], 0)
  • Weighted Medal Score: CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Medals), Medals[Medal] = "Gold") * 3 + CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Medals), Medals[Medal] = "Silver") * 2 + CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(Medals), Medals[Medal] = "Bronze")

Data Sources

  • Competition Data: Paris 2024 Olympic Summer Games Dataset on Kaggle
  • Historical Records: Official Olympic database references via Olympics.com

item.title: Visualizing Microsoft AdventureWorks Data
item.description:
GitHub Repository

Overview

AdventureWorks is Microsoft’s standard relational sample database representing a multinational bicycle manufacturing and retail company. This Power BI dashboard tracks commercial performance across products, sales territories, and customer segments, turning transactional sales records into operational reporting.

The report is organized into three focused pages covering sales volume, target tracking, and customer demographics.

Dashboard Pages

1. Sales Overview

The executive overview summarizes top-line revenue, order counts, return rates, and product category distribution.

  • Revenue by Category: Breaks down total sales across Bikes, Components, Clothing, and Accessories.
  • Geographical Distribution: Maps revenue across sales regions in North America, Europe, and Australia.
  • Returns Tracking: Highlights product categories with above-average return rates to identify potential quality or fulfillment issues.
  • Dynamic Slicers: Allows filtering by product category, subcategory, territory, and transaction date range.

2. Performance Metrics & Target Tracking

This view compares actual monthly operational figures against management targets to monitor pacing and profitability.

  • Actual vs. Target KPIs: Gauge charts and status cards comparing current-month performance against budgeted targets for orders, revenue, and returns.
  • Trend Analysis: Weekly rolling profit and revenue trendlines tracking seasonal fluctuations and growth trajectory.
  • Variance Indicators: Color-coded KPI cards indicating whether key metrics are ahead or behind scheduled goals.

3. Customer Analytics & Segmentation

The customer intelligence page analyzes purchasing habits across demographic attributes to profile core customer cohorts.

  • Income and Occupation: Revenue distribution across annual income brackets and professional occupations (Management, Professional, Skilled Manual, Clerical).
  • Demographic Breakdown: Customer segmentation by age group, marital status, and gender.
  • Purchase Frequency: Tracks average spend per customer and order repetition rates.

Data Model & DAX Measures

The underlying data model follows a star schema connecting transactional fact tables (Sales and Returns) to dimension tables (Customer, Product, Territory, and Calendar).

Key DAX measures include:

  • Total Revenue: SUMX(Sales, Sales[OrderQuantity] * Sales[UnitPrice])
  • Total Profit: [Total Revenue] - SUMX(Sales, Sales[OrderQuantity] * Sales[TotalProductCost])
  • Return Rate %: DIVIDE(COUNT(Returns[ReturnQuantity]), COUNT(Sales[OrderQuantity]), 0)
  • Revenue Variance to Target: [Total Revenue] - [Target Revenue]

Cross-filtering is enabled across all visualizations, and users can drill down from parent product categories into specific product models.

Data Source

  • Dataset: Microsoft AdventureWorks Sample Data

item.title: Starbucks Drinks Dashboard
item.description:
GitHub Repository

Note on Data: This project was developed as an exploratory data visualization study using simulated beverage metrics and location data to model commercial nutritional reporting.

Overview

Modern beverage menus span hundreds of customized variations across milk bases, sweeteners, and portion sizes. This Power BI dashboard provides structured reporting on beverage nutrition, breaking down calorie counts, sugar loads, macronutrient splits, and global store presence across four analytical pages.

Dashboard Pages

1. Beverage Portfolio Overview

The introductory page provides an aggregate view of the beverage menu across major drink categories (Espresso, Brewed Coffee, Frappuccino, Tea, and Cold Brew).

  • Menu Composition: Distribution of drink offerings by category and available cup sizes (Short, Tall, Grande, Venti).
  • Macronutrient Averages: Baseline calorie, protein, fat, and carbohydrate levels averaged by beverage line.
  • Top Ranks: Quick-reference cards highlighting beverages with the highest and lowest calorie counts per category.

2. Nutritional Profiles & Macronutrients

A comparative view breaking down primary dietary macronutrients across drinks.

  • Fat and Protein Comparisons: Scatter plots and grouped bar charts comparing protein content against total fat across dairy and plant-based milk formulations.
  • Serving Size Normalization: Visualizations that adjust metric comparisons based on fluid volume (caloric density per ounce).
  • Category Slicers: Interactive filters enabling users to compare specific drink subcategories side-by-side.

3. Critical Health Indicators & Sugar Mapping

Focuses on dietary risk factors that consumers and health analysts monitor closely: added sugars, sodium, trans fats, and caffeine.

  • Sugar Content Distribution: Identifies beverages that exceed recommended daily sugar intakes in a single serving.
  • Trans & Saturated Fat Flags: Highlights drinks with elevated saturated fat levels resulting from whipped cream or whole milk preparations.
  • Color-Coded Thresholds: Conditional formatting on tables and KPI cards flagging nutritional extremes.

4. Store Distribution Map

Visualizes store network coverage across international territories.

  • Global Footprint: Geographic plot showing store concentrations across regions.
  • Regional Aggregation: Drill-down from continent and country to local market clusters.

Key DAX Calculations

  • Average Calories per Drink: AVERAGE(Beverages[Calories])
  • Sugar-to-Calorie Ratio: DIVIDE(SUM(Beverages[Sugars_g]) * 4, SUM(Beverages[Calories]), 0)
  • High-Sugar Flag: IF(Beverages[Sugars_g] > 30, "Above 30g", "30g or Below")

item.title: Analysis on Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda
item.description:
GitHub Repository

Overview

Calculating the exact count of unique items in a large data stream typically requires maintaining an in-memory hash table of every distinct entry seen so far. As the corpus grows into millions of tokens, memory consumption scales linearly ($O(N)$), creating bottlenecks in streaming and distributed pipelines.

The Flajolet-Martin (FM) algorithm solves this by probabilistically estimating stream cardinality using a fixed, minimal amount of memory ($O(\log N)$ bits). This project applies the Flajolet-Martin algorithm to estimate the unique vocabulary size across the nine volumes of the Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, comparing the probabilistic estimate against exact set cardinality.

The Flajolet-Martin Algorithm

The algorithm estimates distinct elements by tracking the distribution of trailing zeros in hashed bit representations:

  1. Hash Mapping: Each token $w$ in the text stream is hashed to a uniform 32-bit or 64-bit integer $h(w)$.
  2. Trailing Zeros ($\rho$): For each hash value, the algorithm determines $\rho(h(w))$—the number of trailing zeros before the first 1-bit. A hash ending in $k$ zeros occurs with probability $2^{-(k+1)}$.
  3. Maximum Tracking ($R$): The algorithm maintains $R = \max(\rho(h(w)))$ across all processed tokens. If we observe a sequence ending in $R$ trailing zeros, we can infer that roughly $2^R$ unique elements have passed through the stream.
  4. Correction Factor: The raw estimate is adjusted using the Flajolet-Martin correction factor $\phi \approx 0.77351$:

$$\text{Estimated Cardinality} \approx \frac{2^R}{\phi}$$

Variance Reduction (Stochastic Averaging)

A single hash function has significant statistical variance. To produce a stable estimate:

  • The stream is evaluated across $m$ independent hash functions.
  • The hash functions are divided into $g$ distinct groups.
  • The arithmetic mean of estimates is computed within each group.
  • The overall result is obtained by taking the median of group averages, filtering out extreme outlier hash values.

Processing Pipeline

The text processing pipeline handles the multi-volume corpus in Python:

  1. Text Extraction & Cleaning: Reads raw volume texts, stripping metadata, page numbers, and punctuation while normalizing text to lowercase tokens.
  2. Token Streaming: Simulates a continuous token stream rather than holding the entire preprocessed vocabulary in memory.
  3. Multi-Hash Simulation: Generates independent hash functions using linear congruential generators:

$$h_i(x) = (a_i \cdot x + b_i) \pmod p$$

  1. Benchmarking: Compares the FM probabilistic cardinality against standard Python set() counting to evaluate error bounds across different numbers of hash buckets.

Key Insights

  • Memory Efficiency: While exact counting requires storing hundreds of thousands of unique string tokens in memory, the Flajolet-Martin register array requires only a few bytes of storage.
  • Accuracy Trade-off: Increasing the number of hash functions significantly tightens the standard error, bringing the estimated vocabulary count within 5-10% of the true distinct word count.
